$comment: Machine-readable record of the StudioNet proof runs. Every hash here is full and unabbreviated, and every value was read back from the deployed contract rather than transcribed from a console. Re-read any of it with `genlayer call <contract> <method>`, or through genlayer-js with `node scripts/exercise-studionet.mjs <review-id> <request-tx> <review-tx>`. The contract has been redeployed twice; this file records the current deployment first and keeps the superseded ones under historicalDeployments, because their transactions prove the behaviour of those contracts and nothing about this one.

signer.note: Obtained through the CLI's own BaseAction/getClient path and the OS-keychain cache populated by `genlayer account unlock`. No key was exported, no wallet or keystore was created, and no password was supplied on a command line or written to a file.

deployment.gitCommitNote: The commit whose contracts/IntentGuard.py is byte-identical to the retrieved deployed source, not HEAD at the instant of deployment. The deployment was made from the working tree this commit then recorded, so the commit is minutes younger than the transaction above.

parityProof.note: Compared byte-for-byte with no normalisation of either side. The CLI frames the payload with a `Result:` line and two trailing newlines of its own; those framing bytes are asserted rather than stripped, so a real difference could not hide inside them. This is a claim about the contract source, not an independent audit of validator bytecode.

whyRedeployed.defect: The previous deployment read the first four bytes of an action's calldata as its function selector. Governor Bravo stores a named action as a function signature in signatures[i] and the arguments alone in calldatas[i], and the Timelock computes bytes4(keccak256(signature)) at execution time. For a named action those first four bytes are therefore the head of the first argument, and for a leading address they are 0x00000000.
whyRedeployed.impact: Every named action was reported as unnameable, so Rule 5 refused to certify an opaque call and UNDERSPECIFIED was the only verdict the contract could reach on a Compound-shaped proposal. The product's central claim, that it names every call, failed on the majority of real Compound proposals.
whyRedeployed.howFound: By running Compound proposal 294 against the previous deployment for real. It stored the rationale 'All eight actions ... are marked as OPAQUE, with the 4-byte selector 0x00000000 being unconfirmed', while the Governor's own getActions names all eight.
whyRedeployed.fix: _bare_actions now derives a named action's selector from the declared signature and _enrich_action treats that declaration as authoritative, recording name_source as 'governor' rather than 'selector' and telling the model which of the two it is looking at. Regression coverage is tests/direct/test_named_actions.py, ten tests, including one end-to-end round that reaches a real verdict with 4byte answering nothing at all.
whyRedeployed.provenLive: IG-PROOF-3 below is the same proposal on the new deployment. All eight actions now resolve with their real function names.

app.wiring: NEXT_PUBLIC_INTENT_GUARD_CONTRACT is set to the contract above, so the deployed build reads the same StudioNet state recorded in this file rather than the on-disk fixture set. The address is present in the served HTML.
app.loginWall: None. Vercel Deployment Protection was disabled on the project, so every route above answers 200 to an unauthenticated request.
app.corsVerified: https://studio.genlayer.com/api answers an OPTIONS preflight from Origin https://intent-guard-genlayer.vercel.app with access-control-allow-origin echoing that exact origin, so the browser's read path is not blocked from the deployed host.
app.serverSide: None. There is no API route, server action, database, indexer, worker or cron. Reads and writes both go from the browser straight to the GenLayer RPC, and every time transition is a permissionless button.
app.walletMode: Injected only. window.ethereum is the sole signer. There is no generated key, no localStorage key and no local-signer fallback; browser-generated wallets were removed deliberately and are not supported.

lifecycles.$comment: First proof run on the current deployment, 2026-08-23. Compound Governor Bravo, whose proposals use Bravo's named-action shape. This is the proposal that exposed the selector defect on the previous deployment, re-run here against the fix.
lifecycles.mandateTitle: [Gauntlet] Rewards Contract Top-Up for Arb and IR Recs for USDT Mainnet and USDC Arbitrum Comets

transactions.deltaExplanation: One open review bond. stats().bounty_pool is 0 and there are no open rebuttals, so balance = open review bonds holds exactly.

The review settled and the bond was paid back to the requester, so the open-bond term returns to zero. The outbound transfer applies to the ledger asynchronously: eth_getBalance still read 1000000000000000 at the moment the receipt became readable and read 0 once settlement applied, roughly twenty seconds later. Both readings are recorded rather than only the convenient one.

storedState.$comment: Read back on 2026-08-23 through genlayer-js against the contract above.

get_review.mandate_title: [Gauntlet] Rewards Contract Top-Up for Arb and IR Recs for USDT Mainnet and USDC Arbitrum Comets

get_actions.note: This list is the proof of the fix. On the superseded deployment every one of these eight rows carried selector 0x00000000, resolved false and an empty signature.

is_vetoed.note: The mandate was too vague to authorise or exclude what the calls do.

verdict.why: The round matched the mandate's own figures against the decoded arguments: actions #0 to #3 set the four interest-rate slopes on comet 0x3afdc9... to 0.05, 4, 0.052 and 3.6, exactly the values the text lists, and actions #5 to #7 move 13,000 COMP, exactly the top-up the text authorises. It still declined to certify, because action #7's outboundTransferCustomRefund carries a nested payload whose own function cannot be named, and the mandate's claim is about what arrives on Arbitrum. Under Rule 5 an opaque call blocks ALIGNED without being evidence of divergence, so the verdict is UNDERSPECIFIED.
verdict.consequence: The contrast with the superseded deployment is the point. There the rationale was 'All eight actions ... are marked as OPAQUE'; here the rationale reasons about named functions and their actual arguments and lands on UNDERSPECIFIED for one specific nested payload. Same proposal, same rules, a real analysis instead of a blanket refusal.

lifecycles.$comment: Second proof run on the current deployment, 2026-08-23. Uniswap Governor Bravo, whose proposals use Bravo's unnamed-action shape, so this exercises the 4byte-and-keccak path rather than the governor-declared path. Both shapes are covered on the same deployment.

transactions.note: One DISAGREE, recorded as it occurred. The round still finalized and the leader's execution was SUCCESS. A unanimous round would be the surprising result here: these validators fetch mainnet calldata independently and decode it under inference.
transactions.deltaExplanation: Bond settled and paid back, same asynchronous settlement lag as IG-PROOF-3.

verdict.why: Action #0 matches the mandate directly through setProtocolFeeController(address), and actions #1 and #6 are createRetryableTicket relays carrying that same nested call. Actions #2, #4 and #5 wrap cargo the round could not examine, and action #3's selector 0x76ef8453 could not be confirmed. The mandate's claim is about what those relays set on remote PoolManagers, so opaque cargo blocks ALIGNED without proving divergence.
verdict.consequence: A second real proposal on the current deployment, a different Governor, a different action shape and a different naming path, reaching the same PENDING to UNDERSPECIFIED transition. It did not diverge, so the veto, rebuttal and override branches were not driven from it.

invalidPayableProofs.$comment: The invariant these two transactions prove: an invalid payable request creates no state, changes no accounting, and returns the caller's value. StudioNet does not roll a transfer back when GenVM reverts, so the contract cannot rely on a revert to protect the caller. It validates first and, on any user-input failure, refunds and returns a [REJECTED] reason. The on-chain shape of a rejection is therefore FINALIZED with GenVM SUCCESS and a return value beginning [REJECTED], not a failed transaction.

cases.failureMode: unsupported Governor, reached after entry and after the bond had already arrived
cases.returnValue: [REJECTED] Unsupported Governor 0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111. This contract only reviews Governors whose event topic and getActions ABI it has verified: ['0x408ed6354d4973f66138c91495f2f2fcbd8724c3', '0xc0da02939e1441f497fd74f78ce7decb17b66529']
cases.recordProof: get_review("IG-REJECT-1") returns {} after the transaction finalized.

cases.failureMode: invalid state, the target review is UNDERSPECIFIED and carries no veto, reached after entry and after the bond had already arrived
cases.returnValue: [REJECTED] Review IG-PROOF-3 is UNDERSPECIFIED and carries no veto; there is nothing to rebut
cases.recordProof: get_rebuttal("IG-REBUT-1") returns {} and IG-PROOF-3 still reads rebuttal_id "" and contested false after the transaction finalized.

invalidPayableProofs.settlementTiming: Both after-readings were taken once the outbound refunds had applied to the ledger. _pay emits a transfer, and StudioNet applies it asynchronously, so eth_getBalance can still show the value in the contract at the moment the receipt becomes readable. The figures above are the settled ones and the lag is stated rather than hidden.

stats.$comment: Read live on 2026-08-23 with stats() after all six transactions above.
stats.balanceNote: balance is 0 after two complete lifecycles and two funded rejections, because both reviews settled, both bonds were paid back, and neither rejection kept anything. The invariant balance = open review bonds + open rebuttal bonds + bounty pool holds with every term at zero. A settlement or a refund that had silently failed would have left a balance behind.

controls.name: stock-CLI payable control
controls.observation: The same request_review submitted through the unpatched `genlayer write` reached consensus status ACCEPTED while its GenVM execution reverted, and stats.reviews stayed 0.
controls.why: `genlayer write` hardcodes value: 0n, so the bond never arrived and the contract correctly refused the call. Recorded because it is the cleanest available demonstration that consensus status is not application success.

toolingNote.limitation: GenLayer CLI 0.39.2 `genlayer write` hardcodes value: 0n and has no option for gl.message.value. `--fee-value` is not it: parseTransactionFees assigns that to the nested fees.feeValue, while application value is the top-level value parameter of writeContract.
toolingNote.resolution: The payable writes above were sent from a separate local clone of genlayer-cli at tag v0.39.2 with a one-field --value-wei addition that forwards the amount to the value parameter GenLayerJS already accepts. That clone is not part of this repository and no contract change was needed for it.
toolingNote.notAWorkaroundOn: Signing. The patched clone uses the same BaseAction/getClient path and the same OS-keychain cache as the stock CLI. No key was read, exported or logged.

testCounts.note: tests/direct/test_named_actions.py adds the ten regression tests for the selector defect.

ci.note: CI runs on every push, so the commit that adds this block is validated by a later run than any run this block could name. The final run IDs are recorded in docs/SUBMISSION.md against the exact HEAD they ran on.

notProvenOnChain: The veto path. NOT PROVEN LIVE. A veto needs a live mainnet proposal whose executable calls genuinely contradict its own published text. Four real proposals have now been put through the full request_review to review path across deployments, and none diverged. Twenty-three further Compound proposals were screened by action shape and five read in depth; in every one the mandate matched its actions. A DIVERGENT verdict was not forced out of any of them. Covered instead by deterministic tests in tests/direct/test_lifecycle.py and tests/direct/test_named_actions.py, which drive DIVERGENT rounds under mocked inference over ABI bytes the test files encode themselves.

The rebuttal acceptance path. NOT PROVEN LIVE. Only the rejecting branch of rebut has run on chain, in invalidPayableProofs above, because acceptance can only be reached from a standing veto and no live round produced one.
The governance-override branch. NOT PROVEN LIVE, for the same reason.
The bounty payout path. NOT PROVEN LIVE. bounty_pool has been 0 for the life of every deployment, so no payout could occur.

historicalDeployments.$comment: Superseded on 2026-08-23. These transactions prove the behaviour of this contract only. They are kept because they are true, and because two of them are the evidence for the defect that superseded it.
historicalDeployments.supersededBecause: The selector defect described under deployment.whyRedeployed.

defectEvidence.storedRationaleExcerpt: All eight actions ... are marked as OPAQUE, with the 4-byte selector 0x00000000 being unconfirmed
defectEvidence.whyThatIsWrong: The Governor's own getActions names all eight functions. The contract could not see them because it was looking for the selector in the wrong place.

historicalDeployments.$comment: Superseded on 2026-08-22. Its two lifecycles, IG-PROOF-1 and IG-PROOF-2, are recorded here in full rather than deleted, but they prove the behaviour of this contract and say nothing about the current one.
historicalDeployments.supersededBecause: Payable methods raised on invalid input after gl.message.value had already arrived. StudioNet does not roll a transfer back when GenVM reverts, so that value stayed in the contract with no way to retrieve it.
